extraction.name: MathQA
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems annotated with operation programs, enhancing solvable problems from AQuA with fully specified operational programs.
extraction.creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, and Hannaneh Hajishirzi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built from problems in the AQuA dataset and annotated via crowdsourcing with formal operation programs, with additional annotation expansion to similar problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Math problems are first categorized into math domains using term frequencies to prune the search space of possible operations; similar problems are also found by replacing numeric values with generic numbers and using Levenshtein distance for annotation expansion.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers used a dynamic annotation platform to iteratively select operations and arguments until the problem was solved; the platform provided problem descriptions, category-specific operations, valid arguments, automatic intermediate calculations, submission restrictions, quality-control questions, and validation by 3 validators with at least 2 agreeing.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotated programs were validated by requiring at least 2 out of 3 validators to rank the program as valid; validation accuracy was 94.64% across categories, expert evaluation on 500 problems found 92% valid annotations, and expert-crowd validation agreement was 87%.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The source AQuA dataset contains unwanted noise including incorrect solutions, unsolvable problems, incomplete rationales, duplicates, and statistical bias; the representation language is intended to reduce the influence of such bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset omits high-order polynomials and entirely nonnumeric problems, and some problems remain beyond current models, including sequence problems and problems with multiple interpretations; categorization can also be noisy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of neural math word problem solvers that map word problems to operation programs.
